Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 103, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wal-'Asr﴾: That is, the entire span of time (al-dahr).

﴿Inna al-insana﴾: That is, the whole of mankind.

﴿La-fi khusr﴾: That is, in loss and ruin, for his life is his capital; so when he dies without having believed and without having done righteous deeds, he has suffered complete ruin.

﴿Wa-tawasaw bil-haqq﴾: That is, they enjoined one another to hold to the truth in belief, in speech, and in acting upon it.

﴿Wa-tawasaw bil-sabr﴾: That is, they enjoined one another to be patient in holding to the truth in belief, in speech, and in acting upon it.

The meaning of the verses:

The Almighty's saying ﴿By the time﴾: These three verses contain a judgment, one who is judged, and that by which he is judged. The judgment is what the Almighty has decreed concerning man, all of mankind, of loss and ruin. The one judged is man, the son of Adam, and that by which he is judged is ruin for whoever does not believe and does righteous deeds, and profit and salvation from ruin for those who believe, do righteous deeds, enjoin one another to the truth, and enjoin one another to patience. So the Almighty's saying ﴿By the time﴾ is an oath which Allah swears by, and al-'Asr is the entire span of time, its night and its day, its morning and its evening. The answer to the oath is the Almighty's saying ﴿Verily, man is in loss﴾, that is, in deficiency, destruction and ruin, for he lives in toil (kabad) and dies on the way to Hell, and so he loses everything, even the soul that is between his two sides. And His saying ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: these are the ones whom Allah the Exalted excepted from the loss; they are winners, not losers, by their entering Paradise, the abode of happiness. What is meant by faith is belief in Allah and His Messenger and in what the Messenger brought of guidance and the religion of truth; and what is meant by righteous deeds is the obligatory acts, the recommended acts, and the voluntary acts. His saying ﴿And enjoin one another to the truth﴾: that is, to hold to it in belief, and in speech, and in acting upon it, and that is by following the Book and the Sunnah. His saying ﴿And enjoin one another to patience﴾: that is, they enjoin one another to the truth in belief, speech and action, and to patience in that, until one of them dies while believing in the truth, speaking by it, and acting upon what has come in it. Thus Islam is true, the Book is true, and the Messenger is true; by this they believe, act, and enjoin one another to steadfastness upon that until death.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of Surah al-'Asr, for it comprises the path to salvation in three verses; so much so that Imam al-Shafi'i said: "If Allah had sent down to His creation no proof but this surah, it would have sufficed them."

2- Explanation of the fate of the disbelieving person, that it is complete ruin.

3- Explanation of the success of the people of faith and righteous deeds, who avoid shirk and sins.

4- The obligation of enjoining one another to the truth and enjoining one another to patience among the Muslims.
